newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-DVORAK MISSES CHANCE OF WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DVORAK MISSES CHANCE OF WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Czech Tomas Dvorak inherited the mantle of the world's best all-round athlete from Olympic champion Dan O'Brien on Wednesday but missed the chance to take the American's world record.
Dvorak won with a championship record of 8,837 points, taking the lead after the eighth event, the pole vault, and setting six personal bests.
One of them, a throw of 70.34 metres in the penultimate discipline, the javelin, meant that the gold medal was secure.
A world record was in prospect if he set another personal best in the 1,500 but Dvorak opted for the easy life, running a relaxed four minutes 35.40 seconds.
The Olympic bronze medallist said he did not regret easing up and throwing away the chance of a $100,000 bonus for a world record.
"I was playing safe throughout the competition, never experimenting," Dvorak said.
However he did regret the absence of O'Brien, winner of the past three titles, who was unable to compete because of injury.
"Now I know I am one of the world's best athletes, but the victory was a little hollow without O'Brien. We would have had a great battle," Dvorak said.

Dvorak looked a potential champion throughout the competition even though American Chris Huffins held the lead for seven events. Huffins had the galling experience of failing to register a throw in the javelin and did not finish the competition.

Eduard Hamalainen, from Finland, won the silver medal with a national record of 8,730 points. It was only the second time that Hamalainen had pulled on a Finnish vest since changing his allegiance from Belarus at the end of last year.
Germany's Frank Busemann, the Olympic silver medallist, took the bronze with 8,652 points.
